name: Tokyo
summary: Ancient temples next to neon crossings, sushi at dawn, rooftop views from Shibuya Sky and Tokyo Tower, digital art museums and tiny bars in Golden Gai.

months.note: Cold, dry and sunny. Many shops and some sights close Jan 1-3 for New Year.
Coldest, quietest month with low hotel prices; plum blossoms late in the month.
Cherry blossoms usually open in late March, so prices and crowds jump at month's end.
Blossoms into early April; Golden Week (Apr 29-May 5) brings peak prices and packed trains.
After Golden Week the weather is pleasant and prices drop.
Rainy season: humid with frequent drizzle, but fewer crowds and hydrangeas in bloom.
Rainy season ends mid to late July, then hot and humid with festivals and fireworks.
Hottest month. Obon (mid-August) fills transport; typhoons can disrupt travel.
Still hot early on and peak typhoon season.
Comfortable temperatures, though early October is wet.
Autumn leaves peak mid to late November; crisp, clear days.
Dry and sunny with winter illuminations; many businesses close from about Dec 29.

tips.title: Visa-free short stays
tips.body: Visitors from about 70 countries, including the US, UK, Canada, Australia and most of the EU, can visit without a visa, usually for up to 90 days. Check the Foreign Ministry list for your passport.

tips.title: No JESTA needed yet
tips.body: Japan plans an ESTA-style pre-travel authorization called JESTA, now due by fiscal 2028. Nothing is required for trips in 2026.

tips.title: Register on Visit Japan Web
tips.body: Enter your immigration and customs details online before you fly to get QR codes for a faster arrival. It's free.

tips.title: Departure tax is now ¥3,000
tips.body: The International Tourist Tax rose from ¥1,000 to ¥3,000 per traveller on 1 July 2026. It's usually added to your airline ticket.

tips.title: Tax-free shopping is now a refund
tips.body: From 1 November 2026 you pay the full price including 10% tax, then get it refunded after customs checks the goods at the airport. Spend at least ¥5,000 per shop per day and keep your passport handy.

tips.title: Cards are common, but carry yen
tips.body: Most shops take Visa and Mastercard, but small restaurants, shrines and stalls may be cash only. 7-Eleven ATMs accept foreign cards, many around the clock.

tips.title: No tipping
tips.body: Tipping isn't done at restaurants, bars, taxis or hotels and can cause confusion.

tips.title: Get a Suica or PASMO card
tips.body: Tap-on IC cards work on almost all Tokyo trains, subways, buses and convenience stores. Tourists can buy a Welcome Suica at Haneda, Narita and major JR stations, or use the Welcome Suica Mobile app on iPhone.

tips.title: JR Pass only pays off for long trips
tips.body: Since 1 October 2026 the 7-day JR Pass costs ¥53,000. It's worth it only with long shinkansen rides, not for getting around Tokyo.

tips.title: Keep quiet on trains
tips.body: No phone calls on public transport; keep your phone on silent and voices low. Leave priority seats free.

tips.title: Shoes off, trash in your bag
tips.body: Some restaurants, temples and inns ask you to take shoes off, so wear socks without holes. Public bins are rare: carry a small bag for rubbish.

tips.title: Type A plugs, 100V
tips.body: Two flat pins at 100V. Most phone and laptop chargers are fine; hair dryers may not be.

tips.title: Strict medicine rules
tips.body: Amphetamine-based ADHD drugs (like Adderall) are banned, as are pseudoephedrine products such as Sudafed and Vicks inhalers. Up to one month of other prescription medicine is fine; bring the prescription.

tips.title: Earthquakes: install Safety tips
tips.body: The free Safety tips app sends earthquake and tsunami alerts in English. Police 110, fire and ambulance 119.

tips.title: Tap water is safe
tips.body: Tokyo tap water is safe to drink. Vending machines are everywhere for hot summers.

places.name: Senso-ji
places.blurb: Tokyo's oldest temple, dedicated to Kannon, reached through the Kaminarimon gate and the Nakamise shopping street.
places.tip: Go early morning or after dark to beat the crowds.

places.name: Asakusa Culture Tourist Information Center
places.blurb: Kengo Kuma-designed tourist centre opposite Kaminarimon, with a free 8th-floor terrace over Nakamise and Tokyo Skytree.

places.name: Hanayashiki
places.blurb: Japan's oldest amusement park, founded in 1853: a compact retro park right next to Senso-ji.

places.name: Ueno Park
places.blurb: Big public park holding national museums, Ueno Zoo, Toshogu shrine and Shinobazu Pond. Famous for cherry blossoms.

places.name: Tokyo National Museum
places.blurb: Japan's oldest and largest museum, with a vast collection of Japanese and Asian art.

places.name: National Museum of Nature and Science
places.blurb: Japan's national natural history and science museum, with dinosaur skeletons and a Japan gallery.

places.name: National Museum of Western Art
places.blurb: Le Corbusier-designed museum, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, strong on Rodin and French painting.

places.name: Akihabara Electric Town
places.blurb: Tokyo's electronics, anime, manga and gaming district. Chuo-dori closes to cars on Sundays.

places.name: Yurakucho gado-shita izakayas
places.blurb: Smoky yakitori and izakaya joints tucked under the brick railway arches between Yurakucho and Shimbashi.

places.name: Shibuya Sky
places.blurb: Open-air rooftop deck about 230 m up on Shibuya Scramble Square, looking straight down on the crossing.
places.tip: Sunset slots sell out weeks ahead: book online.

places.name: Shibuya Scramble Crossing
places.blurb: The famous all-directions crossing outside Shibuya Station's Hachiko exit.

places.name: MAGNET by Shibuya109 rooftop
places.blurb: Rooftop viewing deck and lounge over the Scramble Crossing, reopened in March 2026 after renovation. Cashless only.

places.name: Takeshita Street
places.blurb: Narrow street opposite JR Harajuku Station packed with youth-fashion shops and crepe stands.

places.name: Tokyu Plaza Harajuku Harakado
places.blurb: Shopping and culture complex at the Jingumae crossing, opened 2024, with a rooftop terrace.

places.name: Meiji Jingu
places.blurb: Shinto shrine to Emperor Meiji and Empress Shoken in a big planted forest beside Harajuku Station.

places.name: Yoyogi Park
places.blurb: One of Tokyo's largest parks, next to Meiji Jingu, popular for weekend picnics and buskers.

places.name: Shinjuku Golden Gai
places.blurb: Six narrow alleys of about 200 tiny bars in low postwar buildings.
places.tip: Many bars charge a cover; some are regulars-only.

places.name: Kabukicho
places.blurb: Shinjuku's nightlife district, home to the Godzilla head on the Toho building.

places.name: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building
places.blurb: Free observation decks on the 45th floor (202 m) of Kenzo Tange's twin-towered city hall.

places.name: UNIQLO Ginza flagship
places.blurb: Uniqlo's 12-floor global flagship on Chuo-dori.

places.name: Ginza
places.blurb: Tokyo's upscale shopping district. Chuo-dori closes to cars on weekend afternoons.

places.name: Kabukiza
places.blurb: Tokyo's main kabuki theatre. Single-act tickets let you watch one act from the top floor.

places.name: Tokyo Tower
places.blurb: 333 m tower from 1958, with a Main Deck at 150 m and a Top Deck at 250 m.

places.name: Zojoji Temple
places.blurb: Head temple of the Jodo sect and burial place of six Tokugawa shoguns, with Tokyo Tower behind it.

places.name: Tsukiji Outer Market
places.blurb: Blocks of seafood, knife and food stalls that stayed in Tsukiji after the wholesale market moved to Toyosu.
places.tip: Many shops close Sundays, holidays and some Wednesdays.

places.name: Toyosu Market
places.blurb: Tokyo's wholesale fish market. Tuna auctions run about 5:30-6:30 am, seen from glass-walled galleries.
places.tip: Closer observation deck is a free lottery: apply the month before.

places.name: National Art Center Tokyo
places.blurb: Kisho Kurokawa's wavy glass exhibition hall. No permanent collection; each show sets its own price.

places.name: Tokyo Skytree
places.blurb: 634 m tower, Japan's tallest structure, with decks at 350 m and 450 m.

places.name: Miraikan
places.blurb: Japan's museum of emerging science, known for its Geo-Cosmos globe and robots.

places.name: teamLab Borderless
places.blurb: Immersive digital art museum at Azabudai Hills where the rooms flow into one another.

places.name: teamLab Planets
places.blurb: Barefoot digital art museum where you wade through water and gardens of light.

places.name: Ryogoku Kokugikan
places.blurb: Tokyo's national sumo arena. Grand tournaments run in January, May and September; nearby stables hold morning practice.

places.name: Tokyo Disneyland
places.blurb: Disney park at Tokyo Disney Resort, next to DisneySea.
places.tip: Dated tickets, sold online; prices change by date.

places.name: Yasukuni Shrine & Yushukan
places.blurb: Shrine founded in 1869 to Japan's war dead, politically controversial; the Yushukan military museum is in its grounds.

places.name: Kitanomaru Park
places.blurb: Park on the old Edo Castle grounds north of the Imperial Palace, known for moat-side cherry blossoms.

places.name: Imperial Palace East Gardens
places.blurb: Free gardens on the site of Edo Castle's inner keep, with the old castle foundations.

places.name: Kyu Asakura House
places.blurb: 1919 wooden house of politician Torajiro Asakura, with a strolling garden on a slope.

places.name: Daikanyama & Ebisu
places.blurb: Laid-back neighbourhoods south of Shibuya with boutiques, cafés and the T-Site bookshop.

places.name: Hamarikyu Gardens
places.blurb: Former shogun's garden with seawater tidal ponds and an island teahouse, under the Shiodome towers.

places.name: Tokyo International Forum
places.blurb: Rafael Viñoly's ship-hull glass hall between Yurakucho and Tokyo Station. Free to walk through.

places.name: Tokyo Station Ramen Street
places.blurb: A row of well-known ramen shops in the basement on the Yaesu side of Tokyo Station.

places.name: Nezu Museum
places.blurb: Pre-modern Japanese and East Asian art in a Kengo Kuma building with a big garden.

places.name: Keisei Skyliner
places.blurb: Reserved-seat express from Narita Airport to Nippori and Keisei-Ueno in about 41 minutes.

places.name: Tokyo Subway Ticket
places.blurb: Unlimited Tokyo Metro and Toei subway rides for 24, 48 or 72 hours. For overseas visitors.

places.name: Narita Airport
places.blurb: Tokyo's main international airport, about an hour east of the city.

places.name: UNPLAN Shinjuku
places.blurb: Design hostel near Shinjuku-sanchome with dorms, private rooms and a ground-floor lounge.

places.name: Hotel Fukudaya
places.blurb: Small traditional ryokan with tatami rooms in a quiet street near Shibuya.

places.name: The Gate Hotel Tokyo by Hulic
places.blurb: Upscale hotel in the Hibiya and Ginza area.

places.name: Aman Tokyo
places.blurb: Luxury hotel at the top of The Otemachi Tower.

places.name: Ichiran Shibuya
places.blurb: Tonkotsu ramen chain known for solo booths and order sheets to customise your bowl.

places.name: La Cocorico Ueno
places.blurb: French bistro known for rotisserie chicken, by Ueno Park.

places.name: Teppanyaki mon cher ton ton
places.blurb: Teppanyaki inside The Peninsula Tokyo where chefs grill wagyu and seafood at the counter.

places.name: Matcha Stand Maruni
places.blurb: Small Tsukiji tea stand whisking matcha to order. Open 8 am-4 pm, closed Wednesdays.

places.name: bills Omotesando
places.blurb: Bill Granger's Sydney café, known for ricotta hotcakes.

places.name: The Pizza Bar on 38th
places.blurb: 38th-floor pizza omakase at Mandarin Oriental Tokyo.

places.name: Gonpachi Nishi-Azabu
places.blurb: Big Edo-style izakaya in a wooden building, linked to the Kill Bill fight scene. Soba, yakitori and grills until late.

places.name: Kyubey Ginza
places.blurb: Edomae sushi in Ginza: omakase and set sushi at the counter.
